haiku-low.q1: 401 Unauthorized is returned. Redis is not called, so no rate-limit budget is used.
haiku-low.q2: Only 100 requests per minute in total for a Standard customer. Counters are keyed by customer ID, so all keys share one budget.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with Retry-After. The backend never sees the request.
haiku-low.q4: No. A rejected request does not increment the count.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. Counting happens inside check_and_incr before forwarding, so the request still counts.
haiku-low.q6: Fail open: one attempt with a 50 ms timeout, no retry. The request is forwarded uncounted, with no X-RateLimit headers, and ratelimit_store_unavailable is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED; the limit is an open question and not set.
haiku-low.q8: One shared Redis, with key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL runs out.
haiku-low.q9: Windows are fixed one-minute UTC-aligned periods. Each new minute uses a new key starting at 0. Old keys expire after 120 s.
haiku-low.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry is made; there is one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers.

sonnet.q1: It gets 401 Unauthorized. Redis is not called, so no counter is affected and no budget is used.
sonnet.q2: Counters are keyed by customer ID, not API key, so all three keys share one budget: the plan's limit per minute in total (Standard 100/min; Enterprise limit not decided).
sonnet.q3: It gets 429 Too Many Requests plus a Retry-After header. The backend never sees the request.
sonnet.q4: No. The count is not incremented on rejection.
sonnet.q5: Yes. Counting happens in check_and_incr before forwarding, so the request still counts even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, forwards the request to the backend without counting it, and returns the response with no X-RateLimit headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard = 100 requests/minute. Enterprise = not decided (open question; Product has not set a limit).
sonnet.q8: In one shared Redis used by all 6 gateway instances, with one counter per customer per minute under key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Redis deletes each key when its 120 s TTL expires; nothing else removes them.
sonnet.q9: Each fixed one-minute window aligned to the UTC clock minute (read from Redis's clock) uses a new key, so the count starts again at 0 at the next minute.
sonnet.q10: check_and_incr is a single Lua script that Redis runs atomically, one script at a time, so two instances can never both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds left until the current minute ends, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry: one attempt with a 50 ms timeout. The client gets the response with no X-RateLimit headers, because the count is unknown.
